summary: Map and gazetteer records place a lookout tower on Woods Mountain, McDowell County, NC; no source found gives its build date, staffing, or condition.

evidence.supports: highest point of the Woods Mountain peaks is 3,646 feet, in NW McDowell County
evidence.quote: NW McDowell County, a series of small peaks. Max. alt. 3,646.

evidence.supports: TopoQuest lists a Woods Mountain Lookout Tower at 3,635 feet MSL (no summit location given)
evidence.quote: and at an elevation of 3635 ft MSL.

evidence.supports: forestry organizations built dozens of lookout structures in Western NC in the 1920s and 1930s as a firefighting system
evidence.quote: In the 1920s and 1930s, forestry organizations built dozens of lookout structures in Western North Carolina as the backbone of a firefighting system.

evidence.supports: Carolina Country review of Barr's guide: lookout towers can be dangerous; many are not routinely maintained
evidence.quote: Lookout towers can be dangerous, and many are not routinely maintained.

evidence.supports: first steel fire towers in the state were built in 1928
evidence.quote: The first steel fire towers in the state were built in 1928.

evidence.supports: CCC constructed numerous towers in the mountains during the 1930s
evidence.quote: constructed numerous towers in the mountains.

evidence.supports: by 1940 North Carolina had a network of fire lookout towers
evidence.quote: By 1940 North Carolina had a network of fire

evidence.supports: towers were typically manned during the fire season, October through May
evidence.quote: Towers were typically manned during the fire season

sources.title: Woods Mountain Lookout Tower, North Carolina
Lookout Towers Played role in Preserving Forests

notes_for_editor: Record status is unknown. Only a TopoQuest map-feature entry and an NCpedia gazetteer entry name this site; neither gives a build date, builder, staffing history or current condition, so the story stops at regional context. Not checked: Peter J. Barr's 2021 guide (possible source on this tower), NC Forest Service or McDowell County records, and the NHLR/FFLOS registers (no cached entry for Woods Mountain). The tnlandforms NC list gives coordinates only (NCT203, 0 bm).
